source.title: Understanding Addition and Subtraction in Transformers
source.authors: P. Quirke; Clement Neo; Fazl Barez

record.tranche_reason: The study measures polysemantic reuse across addition and subtraction in mixed-operation models, a different setting and method from toy-model feature superposition.
record.gate_note: The mixed-model reuse results bear on V3. The reported arithmetic accuracies and carry-circuit analyses do not test feature superposition, capacity competition, SAE completeness, or whether features are one-dimensional; they are not rows for those versions.
record.test_reason: The study never addresses superposition, capacity pressure or sparse features. Its 'polysemantic' nodes are attention heads or MLP layers at a token position. Each computes related arithmetic subtasks (SA, MD, ND) for several operations. This is task-level circuit reuse, a different construct from polysemantic neurons representing unrelated features. No capacity manipulation or control is reported. The authors attribute the reuse to shared task structure by assertion, not by test. So the results do not bear on whether polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure (V3), or on any other version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that mixed models reuse addition circuitry polysemantically for subtraction, whether or not initialized from an addition model. They explain this as natural given the shared structure of the three operations. They explicitly make no transfer claim to frontier LLMs. They do not connect the finding to superposition or capacity.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains and mechanistically analyzes specialized arithmetic transformers; it does not apply the original toy-model feature-superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported pattern varies in implementation across models, including head assignment, redundancy, timing, and delivery route. The study also reports different borrow-delivery arrangements at 6 and 8 digits.

fits_no_version.finding: In mixed addition/subtraction models, most inserted addition nodes come to compute subtasks for two or three question classes (Table 2: 42/48, 40/48, 29/48 inserted nodes per class). Reuse is said to occur from scratch too. Mixed models had more layers/heads than the addition model, but capacity was not varied.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Small transformers trained on structurally similar tasks reuse the same attention heads/MLP layers across tasks (task-level circuit sharing), whether initialized from a single-task model or trained from scratch.

fits_no_version.finding: In one 6-digit mixed model, the two subtraction classes read the resolved borrow along one shared direction (|cos| ≈ 0.9), while the addition carry axis is near-orthogonal (~0.21). Operation selection has no rank-1 direction; patching full selector state flips answers (0.96). Single model and seed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Carried arithmetic data in small transformers is low-dimensional per operation family, near-orthogonal across families, while operation selection is a distributed high-dimensional transformation.

record.problems: Evidence for polysemantic reuse is from specialized models trained on both operations. The table gives detailed reuse counts for a sample model, while the aggregate claim across training setups has no count stated. The paper notes that some sufficiency and restoration results are single-seed, and that the models are not frontier LLMs.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results omitted. General arithmetic accuracy, carry-circuit causal tests, and representation measurements were excluded because they do not measure the versions beyond the mixed-operation node reuse recorded above.

untested.parts: No toy sparse-feature model or feature-geometry measurement.
No manipulation of capacity or feature importance; no dedicated vs shared dimension analysis.
No test of whether polysemantic neurons arise without capacity pressure. Node reuse is not compared across capacity levels, and units are heads/MLP layers, not neurons.
No LLM or SAE experiment. SAEs are only cited.
No test of whether superposed features are 1-D. Low-dimensional carry/borrow directions are not framed as superposed features.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V3 'supports' label is removed. 'Polysemantic' here means a head or MLP at a position computing several operation-specific subtasks. That is not the neuron-level polysemanticity V2/V3 address, and no capacity condition was tested. The subspace-geometry result (cos 0.9 vs 0.21) is recorded under fits_no_version with no row, since it does not test V6.

versions.untested_parts: No sparse-feature toy-network experiment or measurement of overlapping, nearly orthogonal feature directions or a sparsity-dependent geometric transition.
The study does not test whether capacity pressure causes polysemanticity, or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions while others share.

Tests reuse across arithmetic operations in specialized mixed models, not the prevalence of polysemantic neurons in ordinary LLMs or whether such units are evidence of superposition in other settings.
No LLM feature-spreading or SAE-recovery experiment.
No test of whether dictionary features are complete, stable, or canonical.
No test comparing one-dimensional with multidimensional superposed features.

rows.measure: Polysemantic reuse of addition circuitry across operations
rows.value: The authors report that nodes become polysemantic and that reuse occurs whether the mixed model is trained from scratch or initialized from an addition model; no aggregate count is stated.
rows.note: The study reports shared task computation in attention/MLP nodes; it does not report a count of individual polysemantic neurons.
rows.check: Measures multi-operation reuse of nodes (heads/MLPs at positions), not polysemantic neurons or their cause. No count is given. The from-scratch claim is stated in words only ('arises whether or not the mixed model is initialized'). There is no capacity baseline, so it cannot bear on V3.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Mixed addition-and-subtraction models; the reported initialized-model example and the authors' aggregate statement about both training setups
reader_labels.reason: The study reports nodes reused across operation subtasks, including 42/48 for addition, 40/48 for positive-answer subtraction, and 29/48 for negative-answer subtraction in the sample model (R1–R4). This shows polysemantic reuse in a setting with multiple trained operations, without establishing capacity pressure as its cause.
